designedAgainst.note: Design only, per the master contract's blueprint-before-content rule. No runtime module imports this file; nothing here is available to a learner. Product availability stays false until a separate release gate.

prerequisiteReconciliation.rule: B1 cannot name exact A2 capability ids with certainty because A2's own blueprint is authored in a parallel lane and has not landed yet. Every A2-facing prerequisite below is an EXPECTED A2 exit capability, derived only from the master contract's own description of A2 (curriculum-master-a1-c2.md section 4) and from the exact ids A1 already coined for its own deferredToA2 list in docs/curriculum/a1-blueprint.json. This keeps the coupling honest: nothing here is invented from memory of a syllabus, and every expected id is traceable to a document already in the repo.

expectedA2ExitCapabilities.meaning: narrate a single past event or day, sentence by sentence, in simple past
state a near-future plan or arrangement using going to
add one clause of reason to a statement using because
compare two things using one comparative form
describe a person or place using more than one attribute

expectedA2ExitCapabilities.source: coined from master contract section 4 (A2 includes "everyday problems"); no exact A1-coined id exists for this one
expectedA2ExitCapabilities.meaning: understand and give a short reaction to a stated everyday problem, without yet having to resolve it unaided

expectedA2ExitCapabilities.source: coined from master contract section 4 (A2 includes "longer exchanges"); no exact A1-coined id exists for this one
expectedA2ExitCapabilities.meaning: sustain a single-topic exchange longer than A1's 10-12 turn ceiling, still on one topic

A mismatch (missing capability, different id, weaker evidence type) is a cross-level defect to fix before LC-FND-002, not a B1 defect to silently work around.

exact id, but A2 scope=should not required — see sustain_topic_change.prerequisiteRisk (F4b)

canDo: narrate a personal experience as a connected sequence of past events, including one that was interrupted by another
give an opinion about something familiar with a reason, and agree or disagree with someone else's opinion politely
compare more than two options on more than one quality and justify a preference
describe a place, event or service in enough detail for someone else to decide whether to go, and recommend or warn them
explain what is wrong in an everyday problem clearly enough for someone to help, and negotiate a solution
talk about plans, intentions and predictions, distinguishing a spontaneous decision from a fixed plan
say what they hope or would like to do, beyond a scheduled plan
say what will happen under a real, likely condition
keep a conversation going across more than one topic: change subject politely, ask a genuine follow-up question, and summarize what someone else said
cannotYet: sustain a formal register or switch register deliberately
use the present perfect, past perfect or any perfect aspect
build a full second or third conditional, or a mixed conditional
construct an extended argument with counter-arguments and concession chains
use modals of deduction and speculation (must be, can't have been)
handle abstract or specialist topics outside everyday experience
self-correct register or nuance without being prompted
definition.interactionCeiling: one to two related topics per conversation, natural topic changes allowed, 12-16 meaningful turns, flexible use of known language rather than fixed frames, support fades to hints-on-request by default and is restored quickly after repeated strain

canDos.canDo: tell a short personal story as a connected sequence of past events, not a list of separate sentences
cefrRefs: B1 Spoken Production (global scale): can connect phrases in a simple way in order to describe experiences and events
B1 Coherence: can link a series of shorter, discrete simple elements into a connected, linear sequence of points
canDos.why: A2 can narrate one past event; B1's shift is from isolated statements to a held sequence, which is the connective tissue every later narrative-shaped capability in the level reuses.
reuseContexts: somethings_wrong arc (narrating how a problem started)
transferContexts: a story about a weekend or trip never rehearsed sentence-by-sentence in training
canDos.independentEvidence: two connected narrations of at least three clauses each, unaided, each using at least two different sequence connectors
canDos.delayedRetrieval: capstone arc recall of a story told earlier in the level, without connectors being re-taught

canDos.canDo: say what was happening when something else happened, contrasting an ongoing past action with an interrupting event
cefrRefs: B1 Grammatical accuracy: can use reasonably accurately a repertoire of frequently used routines and patterns associated with more predictable situations
canDos.why: The commonest genuinely new B1 narrative shape: a background action broken by an event is how real stories are told, and it is the level's only new past-tense form.
reuseContexts: describe_an_experience (an interruption inside a described event)
transferContexts: a story with an interruption the learner chooses themselves, not one of the taught examples
canDos.independentEvidence: two unaided sentences that correctly contrast an ongoing action with an interrupting event
canDos.delayedRetrieval: capstone recall, at least one session after the home episode

canDos.canDo: state a simple opinion about something familiar and give one reason for it
cefrRefs: B1 Spoken Interaction (global scale): can enter unprepared into conversation on topics that are familiar
B1 Discussion descriptor: can give or seek personal views and opinions in an informal discussion with friends
B1: can briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions, plans and actions
canDos.why: Everyday independence at B1 means having a stance, not only reporting facts about oneself. This is the level's first genuinely evaluative speech act.
transferContexts: an opinion about a topic the episode never modeled an opinion sentence for
canDos.independentEvidence: two unaided opinion-plus-reason statements on two different topics
canDos.delayedRetrieval: reused unprompted inside the which_one and looking_ahead arcs, sessions later

canDos.canDo: agree or disagree with someone else's stated opinion, politely, with a reason
cefrRefs: B1 Discussion descriptor: can generally follow the main points of extended discussion... and express agreement/disagreement
canDos.why: An opinion nobody can respond to is a monologue. This is what turns give_an_opinion into a real exchange, and it is the level's main politeness-under-disagreement skill.
reuseContexts: somethings_wrong arc (disagreeing with a proposed solution)
transferContexts: disagreeing with an opinion phrased in a way not seen during teaching
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided agreement and one unaided disagreement, each with a reason, on two different opinions

canDos.canDo: compare more than two things using more than one quality and say which they prefer, with a reason
cefrRefs: B1: can compare and contrast alternatives, discussing what to do, where to go, who or which to invite, etc.
canDos.why: A2 compares two things on one quality. B1's shift is genuinely flexible comparison: several options, several attributes, a justified choice rather than a fixed frame.
transferContexts: comparing three options the episode never modeled together
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided comparison of three or more options across at least two qualities, ending in a justified choice
canDos.delayedRetrieval: reused unprompted inside recommend_or_warn, sessions later

canDos.canDo: describe a place, event or service they experienced, with more than one attribute, including how it made them feel
cefrRefs: B1 Spoken Production: can give straightforward descriptions on a variety of familiar subjects within their field of interest
B1: can describe experiences and reactions in simple connected text
canDos.why: A2 describes a person or place with one attribute. B1 needs a description rich enough to be useful to someone deciding whether to go, which requires holding several attributes and an evaluative reaction together.
reuseContexts: somethings_wrong arc (describing what a broken/wrong thing was like)
transferContexts: describing an experience with an attribute combination not modeled together before
canDos.independentEvidence: two unaided descriptions each using at least two attributes and one feeling/reaction word
canDos.delayedRetrieval: reused unprompted inside recommend_or_warn, sessions later

canDos.canDo: recommend or warn someone based on their own comparison or experience
cefrRefs: B1: can give advice on a simple matter within their competence, and can ask for and follow detailed directions or advice
canDos.why: Comparison and description are only useful to a real listener if they end in a recommendation. Kept as should-have: the core independence of the arc is already evidenced by the two required capabilities it draws on.
transferContexts: a recommendation about something the two prerequisite capabilities were exercised on separately, never together
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided recommendation and one unaided warning, each grounded in a stated reason

canDos.canDo: explain clearly what is wrong in an everyday situation (wrong order, broken thing, delay, lost item) so someone else can help
cefrRefs: B1: can explain what is wrong with something
B1 Spoken Interaction: can deal with most situations likely to arise when travelling or making arrangements
canDos.why: A2 can respond to a problem someone else names (respond_to_a_simple_problem, an internally-coined expected id superseded by A2's real report_a_problem once LC-BP-A2 landed). B1's independence step is initiating and framing the problem clearly enough that a stranger who was not there can act on it.
transferContexts: a problem type not modeled during teaching (a different broken item or a different kind of delay)
canDos.independentEvidence: two unaided problem statements, each naming what is wrong and what was expected instead
canDos.delayedRetrieval: capstone recall, a different problem than the one taught

canDos.canDo: ask for and negotiate a solution (replacement, refund, reschedule), accepting or politely pushing back on what is offered
cefrRefs: B1: can negotiate to sort out a problem, e.g. an unjustified bill in a hotel
canDos.why: Reporting a problem without resolving it leaves the learner exactly where A2 already leaves them. This closes the interaction, and it is the level's clearest test of flexible, non-scripted negotiation.
transferContexts: negotiating an outcome the episode did not offer as one of its scripted options
canDos.independentEvidence: one whole negotiation held unaided from stating the problem to accepting or countering a solution
canDos.delayedRetrieval: capstone recall with a different offered solution

canDos.canDo: show mild disappointment or frustration without being rude, and stay cooperative
cefrRefs: B1 Pragmatic competence (register, informal): can maintain a cooperative tone while expressing a negative reaction to a familiar person
canDos.why: A negotiation held with flat politeness only is not how people actually sound. Should-have: it is a tone layer on escalate_and_resolve_a_problem, not a new communicative function.
canDos.firstContext: somethings_wrong arc, second episode (layered onto negotiate_a_solution's practice)
transferContexts: a frustration phrase chosen freely rather than the one modeled
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided use of a frustration phrase that keeps the conversation cooperative rather than closing it
canDos.delayedRetrieval: not separately tracked; observed inside negotiate_a_solution's delayed retrieval

canDos.canDo: talk about plans and intentions, and make quick decisions or predictions, choosing correctly between will and going to
cefrRefs: B1: can talk about plans, arrangements and doing things in the near future
B1: can make predictions about likely future events
canDos.why: A2 has one future form (going to) for fixed plans. B1's shift is choosing between a fixed plan, a spontaneous decision and a prediction, which is a genuinely new judgment, not new vocabulary.
transferContexts: choosing will vs going to for a situation not modeled during teaching
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided spontaneous decision, one unaided prediction, and one unaided fixed plan, each using the correct form

canDos.canDo: say what they hope, want or would like to do in the future, beyond a scheduled plan
cefrRefs: B1 Spoken Production (global scale): can connect phrases in a simple way in order to describe... dreams, hopes and ambitions
canDos.why: This is the exact global-scale B1 descriptor the level is named for. A plan has a date; a hope does not, and distinguishing the two is the point.
transferContexts: a hope about a topic never modeled as an example sentence
canDos.independentEvidence: two unaided hope/ambition statements on two different topics
canDos.delayedRetrieval: capstone recall, a session after the home episode

canDos.canDo: say what will happen if a real, likely condition is met
cefrRefs: B1 Grammatical accuracy: can use some simple structures correctly, e.g. the first conditional
canDos.why: First conditional is the cheapest new structure in the arc: it reuses will from talk_about_plans_and_intentions and adds one clause shape. Should-have because the arc's required independence is already evidenced by plans and hopes.
reuseContexts: negotiate_a_solution reuse (a conditional offer, e.g. "if you can't replace it, I'd like a refund")
transferContexts: a real-condition sentence about a situation not modeled during teaching
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided if-clause sentence with a correct real-condition structure

canDos.canDo: give simple advice or imagine a hypothetical situation using a basic If I were you frame
cefrRefs: B1+: can speculate about alternatives using simple hypothetical language (Companion Volume extension beyond core B1; kept optional for that reason)
canDos.why: A light preview of B2's hypothetical reasoning, kept to one fixed frame so it does not become an early second conditional. Optional: the level's required independence never depends on it.
reuseContexts: the_long_conversation capstone, only if the learner has evidenced it
transferContexts: advice about a situation the learner names themselves, not one of the taught examples
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided use of the If I were you frame giving advice on a self-chosen situation
canDos.delayedRetrieval: not required for graduation; observed opportunistically

canDos.canDo: keep a conversation going across more than one topic, changing the subject politely and following someone else's change
cefrRefs: B1 Spoken Interaction: can enter unprepared into conversation on familiar topics
B1 Turntaking: can intervene in a discussion... using an appropriate phrase to get the floor
canDos.why: Every earlier B1 capability is still exercised inside one topic. This is the level's discourse-level shift: a conversation that moves, the way A1 and A2 conversations deliberately do not.
canDos.prerequisiteRisk: keep_a_longer_conversation_going is A2 scope=should, not required, so not every graduating A2 learner is guaranteed to have produced it independently (LC-AUD-001 F4b). This required B1 capability must not assume that evidence exists: the keep_talking arc's first episode provides a first-exposure bridge (a model turn changing topic, not withheld the way an already-evidenced prerequisite would be) for a learner who never independently evidenced the A2 should-capability, consistent with the shared scaffolding engine reacting to genuinely low prerequisite evidence rather than assuming it (curriculum-master-a1-c2.md section 10).
transferContexts: changing to a topic the conversation partner raises unexpectedly
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided topic change initiated by the learner, and one unaided follow of a partner-initiated change
canDos.delayedRetrieval: capstone recall inside a conversation touching three or more topics

canDos.canDo: ask a natural follow-up question that shows genuine interest, not just answer and stop
cefrRefs: B1: can ask follow-up questions to check they have understood what a speaker wanted to say
canDos.why: A conversation that only answers is still an interview, the exact ceiling A1 and A2 leave in place. This is what makes it feel mutual.
transferContexts: a follow-up question about something a partner said that the episode never modeled a question for
canDos.independentEvidence: two unaided follow-up questions on two different partner statements

canDos.canDo: briefly restate what someone else said, to check understanding or pass it on to someone else
cefrRefs: B1 Mediation: can pass on the basic content of straightforward informative material to another person
canDos.why: The level's clearest mediation-shaped task in Nation's Four Strands sense. Should-have: the arc's required independence is already evidenced by topic change and follow-up questions.
transferContexts: summarizing content the episode did not provide a summary template for
canDos.independentEvidence: one unaided summary of a partner turn at least two sentences long

deferredToB2.why: Weighing advantages/disadvantages with counter-arguments needs concession language (however, on the other hand, admittedly) B1 does not yet have as a productive structure.
Connecting past to present (experience, result, unfinished time) is a distinct aspect from simple past narration and deserves its own arc rather than riding in on narrate_connected_event.
No B1 required capability needs an unknown agent; every B1 problem/negotiation names who did what.
Backshift and reporting verbs are a system of their own; summarize_what_was_said covers the B1-appropriate mediation need without full reported speech.
imagine_a_hypothetical keeps one fixed frame deliberately; a productive second conditional plus a third conditional is B2-scale grammar load.
Register control (I suppose, sort of, to some extent) matters once B2 assesses pragmatic appropriateness explicitly; B1 stays informal throughout.
Polite indirect framing (Could you tell me where...) is a politeness upgrade on structures B1 already has direct forms for; not required for B1 independence.
must be / can't have been is inference language for evidence B1 conversations do not yet require the learner to weigh.

optionalOrNotTaken.why: Multiple narrators in one story is a discourse-coordination load beyond what sustain_topic_change already covers at B1.
The product is conversational; a written formal register belongs with any future writing-mode work, not spoken B1.
Available as a neutral topic inside discourse_management arcs; not a required capability because it depends on real-world content the product does not curate.

proposed.whyNotExisting: A problem is an issue attached to a thing or event, not the thing itself; a slot that accepts it must refuse a plain object with nothing wrong with it, which generic_object cannot express ('there's a problem with a book' has no content until the book has something wrong with it).

explicitlyNotNeeded.why: B1 stays informal throughout; register control is a B2 assessment dimension, not a B1 slot.
imagine_a_hypothetical reuses person/activity; the fixed if_i_were frame needs no new noun type.
sustain_an_argument is deferred to B2; B1 opinions are single-clause reasons, not structured positions.

intentStrategy.rule: Inherits the A1 rule unchanged: one intent per communicative function. Variants travel as a subtype on the step payload, not as a new intent.

newSubtypesOnExistingIntents.note: carries narrate_connected_event vs narrate_interrupted_action; both are one communicative function (telling what happened), two forms
carries express_frustration_politely as a tone layer on escalate_and_resolve_a_problem, not a separate speech act

counts.a1PlusA2IntentsAssumed: not fixed until A2 lands; B1 adds its own 14 regardless of the exact prior total

intentStrategy.explosionGuard: Same rule as A1: an arc needing more than three new intents is teaching phrases rather than a capability. Verified per arc in the arcs list below; the densest B1 arcs (which_one, looking_ahead, keep_talking) sit at exactly three.

evaluationStrategy.rule: The canonical frame is always judged locally first, exactly as A1 and Pre-A1 do; escalation is for a reply the local evaluator marks inconclusive. No capability is designed to depend on the provider being reachable.
evaluationStrategy.densityFinding: B1 is materially more hybrid than A1 (13 of 14 new intents vs A1's 3 of 14): the level's whole point is flexible, non-fixed-frame language, so far fewer capabilities can be judged by a small canonical set of correct strings. This is a finding for section 15, not a design shortcut — every hybrid intent still needs a real, testable local fallback that does not silently pass or silently fail an offline learner.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can narrate one past event as separate sentences, but cannot connect a sequence, and cannot say what was already happening when something else happened.
arcs.whyNow: The smallest step from A2's single-event narration, and it establishes the connective and aspectual language every later narrative-shaped reuse in the level draws on.

miniStory.why: A narrated day-out or trip is the natural host for sequence and interruption together, and it gives the learner several structurally similar sentences to build their own version from.

arcs.autonomyTarget: the model narration is visible while the connectors are new and withheld on the arc's last recall
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided connected narrations, at least one containing an interruption
arcs.risk: Past continuous invites over-teaching as a grammar topic. The budget stays anchored to one interruption per story, never a tense drill.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can state facts about themselves but cannot take a position on something and defend it, and cannot respond to someone else's position without just restating their own.
arcs.whyNow: Cheap in new grammar (one frame, one connector already partly known from A2's express_an_opinion_with_a_reason) and it unlocks every later capability that needs a justified stance.

miniStory.why: The value is a live two-way exchange of positions, which roleplay carries better than a narrated scene.

arcs.autonomyTarget: support fades quickly; the opinion frame is one sentence shape reused across the arc
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided opinions with reasons, one unaided agreement, one unaided disagreement
arcs.risk: Opinions on real controversial topics are out of scope for the product. Topics stay neutral (a place, an activity, a piece of media) so the language is exercised without importing debate content the curriculum does not own.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can compare two things on one quality but not choose flexibly among several, cannot describe an experience richly enough for someone else to act on, and cannot turn either into a recommendation.
arcs.whyNow: It reuses the opinion frame just learned as the justification layer for both comparison and description, and it is the arc where opinion becomes useful to a listener.

miniStory.why: A described trip or place carried by a hosted narrator gives the learner several rich descriptions to draw a comparison and a recommendation from.

arcs.autonomyTarget: mid-level: description support fades first, recommendation keeps a hint the longest since it composes two other capabilities
arcs.evidenceTarget: one unaided multi-option comparison, two unaided rich descriptions, one unaided recommendation or warning
arcs.risk: The arc's heaviest vocabulary load. The budget is spent on evaluative adjectives that transfer across many places and events, not on any one topic's specialist words.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner can respond when someone else names a problem but cannot raise one themselves clearly enough to be helped, and cannot negotiate past a first offer.
arcs.whyNow: It needs the reason-giving and (dis)agreement language from i_think_that, and the description language from which_one to say what was expected instead of what happened.

miniStory.why: A problem-and-resolution situation is the arc's clearest whole transaction, and a hosted story can carry the other side's turns while the learner keeps the decisions.

arcs.autonomyTarget: late: the suggestion is withheld on the arc's integrated negotiation episode
arcs.evidenceTarget: two unaided problem statements, one whole negotiation held unaided, one unaided use of a frustration phrase that stays cooperative
arcs.risk: Rudeness. Every model turn stays firmly on the polite side of the ceiling, and express_frustration_politely is explicitly evaluated on staying cooperative, not just on the words used.

arcs.communicativeProblem: The learner has one future form for fixed plans and cannot make a spontaneous decision, a prediction, state a hope with no date attached, or say what happens if something else does.
arcs.whyNow: Independent of the description/problem branch, and it is where the level's grammatical accuracy demand peaks: three related but distinct future-facing judgments in one arc.

miniStory.why: The value is in the learner's own future, not a narrated scene about someone else's.

arcs.autonomyTarget: late: model answers withheld by default, hints on request; imagine_a_hypothetical always keeps a hint since it is optional
arcs.evidenceTarget: one unaided decision, one unaided prediction, one unaided fixed plan, two unaided hope statements, one unaided real-condition sentence
arcs.risk: The level's densest grammar arc. will vs going to is the one genuine architectural risk: the evaluator must judge intent (decision vs plan vs prediction) from context, not from surface form alone, since going to and will can both be grammatically well-formed for the wrong function.

arcs.communicativeProblem: Every capability so far is still exercised inside one topic held by the episode. The learner cannot move a real conversation, follow someone else moving it, or show they were actually listening.
arcs.whyNow: It needs topics worth changing between, which only exist once the level has taught several (an experience, a problem, a plan) — this arc is where they get to coexist in one exchange.

miniStory.why: This is the arc where the conversation itself is the content; a hosted narration would replace the discourse skill being taught with a comprehension task.

arcs.autonomyTarget: late: unaided by default across the whole arc
arcs.evidenceTarget: one unaided learner-initiated topic change, one unaided follow of a partner-initiated change, two unaided follow-up questions, one unaided summary
arcs.risk: Discourse-level evaluation is qualitatively different from single-turn evaluation: judging whether a topic change was natural, or a follow-up question genuine, needs conversational context the evaluator may not currently carry. Flagged in section 15 rather than assumed solvable.

arcs.communicativeProblem: No new problem: this arc proves the six before it add up to one flexible learner rather than six separate skills, by holding all of them inside a single extended, multi-topic conversation nobody scripted turn-by-turn.
arcs.whyNow: Last, deliberately, exactly as A1's making_arrangements closes that level: it introduces nothing of its own and earns its place only if the learner leaves able to do what the arc's name says.
reinforcedCanDos: all thirteen required B1 capabilities, plus should-haves the learner has already evidenced

miniStory.why: The level's closing situation: a single extended conversation that starts on one topic, changes at least twice, and surfaces a small problem along the way, with genuinely branching partner turns.

arcs.autonomyTarget: unaided throughout; support only after a wrong answer, matching A1's making_arrangements precedent
arcs.evidenceTarget: delayed retrieval of every required B1 capability inside one held conversation, with at least one genuine topic change and one unplanned problem
arcs.risk: Could become a review episode with a new label, exactly the risk A1's closing arc names about itself. It earns its place only if the conversation branches realistically rather than replaying the level's greatest hits in a fixed order.

counts.note: Global episode ids are not assigned here. They depend on A2's own episode count, which is not yet fixed (LC-BP-A2 has not landed). Numbering is a cross-level integration decision, not a B1 blueprint decision.

legend.D: delayed retrieval, at least one session after the home episode
